name: Babylonian
description: Constellations of the Babylonian MUL.APIN star catalogue, including the Moon-path stations that preceded the zodiac.
source: Wikipedia, "MUL.APIN" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MUL.APIN (sources: Hunger & Pingree 1989; Hoffmann 2017; Rogers 1998)
Figures reuse the IAU constellation stick figures in constellations.json (d3-celestial, BSD-3-Clause; HYG, CC BY-SA 4.0); extra stars from HYG v4.1
license: Wikipedia text: CC BY-SA 4.0; HYG v4.1 data CC BY-SA 4.0. Stellarium has no Babylonian sky culture. Omissions: the Three Ways of Enlil/Anu/Ea are declination bands (>+17, +-17, <-17 deg) without star figures, so they are not drawn; Tails/Great Swallow/Anunitu are only partly identified and skipped.

figures.name: Pleiades
figures.story: Listed in the Babylonian "Path of the Moon" (MUL.APIN, c. 1000 BCE) as MUL.MUL, identified with "The Star Cluster (Star of Stars)". Marker lines connect the identified stars.

figures.name: Bull of Heaven
figures.story: Listed in the Babylonian "Path of the Moon" (MUL.APIN, c. 1000 BCE) as GU4.AN.NA, identified with Taurus and Hyades. Lines are borrowed from the modern constellation of the identification; the Babylonian outline itself is not recorded, so treat it as an approximation of the star area.
